newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - DEC 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - DEC 23.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The road blocks may have gone but the problems remain: farmers removed their tractors from the nation's roads over the weekend but vowed to return in the event their demands were not satisfied. The government stressed there were no 'victors and vanquished' and prepared for talks, as it braced for more protests from other groups.

--The road blocks may have gone but new barricades are being set up at conservative opposition New Democracy. ND leader Miltiades Evert yesterday rebuffed suggestions from his main challenger George Souflias that the forthcoming party congress be made up of the rank and file of the party. Souflias warned of more adventures for the embattled opposition party.

--Seven hundred families around Greece will open their homes to young orphans of the Bosnian war and the dissolution of former Yugoslavia. The orphans - who had spent seven months with Greek families last year - returned over the weekend to spend Christmas in Greece with their foster families.

--Greece's former king, Constantine, said he was confident he would return to Greece as he attended the baptism of his first grandchild. Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew conducted the service at the patriarchate at the Phanar. Britain's Prince Charles was one of Maria-Olympia's godfathers.

--George Souflias warns that a party congress that does not express the rank and file of the party will be the beginning of the end for New Democracy. If the party cannot solve its problems, the current situation of internal party bickering will continue, he says, adding that, with Miltiades Evert at the helm, ND cannot win elections.
